newsitem.title: GERMANY: Early Lufthansa wage talks fruitless.
newsitem.headline: Early Lufthansa wage talks fruitless.

text.p: The first round of wage talks between Deutsche Lufthansa AG and its main unions ended without any clear result on Monday, a spokeswoman for one of the two unions said.
The spokeswoman for the OeTV public service union added that the talks were due to resume on September 25.
With wide differences of opinion between the airline and the unions, both of which have already rejected the airline's call for a pay freeze, no early conclusion to the wage negotiations is seen.

Lufthansa, up against tough competition and a price war in its main markets, has already said that it believed sector conditions meant that it should in principle be seeking to cut its overall wage costs.
Worker representatives have been further alarmed by press reports that the airline was interested in putting out some of its services to franchise, thus reducing its headcount of permanent staff.
OeTV said last week it would be negotiating for a 12-month wage pact based around 2.3 percent rise in wages and said it would be asking for a strengthening of guarantees on jobs protection.
Lufthansa insists that it could only provide guarantees on matters such as job protection within a settlement that would allow it to plan staff costs three years ahead.
German white collar union DAG, whose first round of talks with the airline are due to carry on until Monday evening, has said it would be demanding a four percent pay rise.
It is also determined that Lufthansa be prevented either from franchising out any of its services or and shifting some of them to wage-cost centres abroad.
